result.lens: Operator risk and value: what most misleads or harms the Entra admin (false all-clear audits, mutations whose reported outcome differs from what landed, data loss or duplication, inert documented controls, session and secret handling), then the enhancements that most change what an admin can do.

top.title: Tenant-wide mailbox read/write/export via MailboxItem.*, MailboxFolder.*, Mail-Advanced.* scores zero and raises no mailbox finding
top.why: This is the exact class the audit exists to catch: an app holding Graph Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All or MailboxItem.ImportExport.All (common in backup products, rising as EWS retires) gets a healthy row, no Scope fix and no high-risk points. The fallback whose own comment promises to catch unknown mailbox permissions cannot match these names.
top.where_to_start: crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/scoping.rs:194 extend mailbox_named to Mailbox*/Mail-* prefixes (or a table from Microsoft's RBAC-for-Applications roles) and add the write/export values to HIGH_RISK_APP_PERMISSIONS at crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/audit/permissions.rs:67 with a table test citing the Learn page; then decide whether graph_mail_role gains them (CHANGELOG note per exchange-scoping.md:46-49) or the unconfinable_other text stops claiming RBAC has no role.

top.title: Restore is non-idempotent while the DR view and the restore report both tell the operator to re-run it
top.why: In the one scenario DR exists for, following the on-screen remedy creates a second copy of every already-restored app with new appIds, paired SPs, fresh 180-day secrets and re-granted admin consent, and the Restore button stays live after a successful run. Irreversible without manual cleanup and it multiplies consented trust in the destination tenant.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/dr.rs:502 reword the callout and clear plan/loaded after report.set (dr.rs:168) so the button needs a fresh file load; apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/restore.rs:751 stop saying 're-run the restore' and add an MI-only re-bind action; then make Pass 1 (restore.rs:197) adoption-aware by display name plus a source marker.

top.title: Exchange scoping section toasts 'Migrated' on a partial, incomplete or unattempted AAP migration report
top.why: The backend marks the KEPT-legacy-policy fail-closed path as status partial inside an Ok item, so the Permissions-tab surface toasts success, reloads and never mounts the report. The operator walks away believing the app is confined by RBAC when the legacy policy is the only thing still confining it. The sibling audit dialog gates correctly, so the two surfaces disagree today.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/web-rs/src/components/exchange_scoping_section.rs:324 replace the failures-only gate with a shared AapMigrationReport::is_clean() (dto exchange.rs:174) that requires !incomplete, unattempted.is_empty(), non-empty items and all status == migrated; use it in views/dialogs/migrate_legacy_scope.rs:81 too and fix the toast noun (items are per app).

top.title: SSO tab renders an unreadable claims policy as an empty editor; Save then detaches the real policy and leaks an orphan per save
top.why: Every first-time operator lacks the Policy.ReadWrite consent, so the read is silently swallowed into None and the editor shows empty claims for an app that has a custom policy. One Save (even after granting consent, which does not reload) detaches the configured policy and replaces it with the empty state. Each save also orphans a tenant-level claimsMappingPolicy because the code unassigns and recreates instead of PATCHing.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sso/mod.rs:510 add a claims_read_failed discriminator to SsoConfigDto instead of collapsing Err to (None, None); apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/enterprise_application_detail_pane/sso_tab.rs:543 render a warn Callout with a Load-claims consent button and disable Save until a successful read; then in set_claims_mapping (mod.rs:1643) propagate the listing error with ? and PATCH the existing policy in place when this SP is its sole appliesTo subject.

top.title: The documented auto-update opt-out is inert and MSI/.deb installs are offered the NSIS/AppImage payload
top.why: README tells MDM/CI operators and MSI deployers to rely on AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE / auto_update to avoid a conflicting NSIS install; nothing reads the flag, so every launch egresses to GitHub and an MSI operator who clicks 'Update & restart' gets a second per-user install beside the per-machine one; a .deb install downloads the AppImage and fails with a raw plugin string. A documented security control that does nothing is the worst kind.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/updater.rs:26 gate check_for_update and perform_update on UserSettings::load(&config_directory()).auto_update and on tauri::utils::platform::bundle_type() (short-circuit Msi/Deb/Rpm); make the result a tri-state (UpToDate / Available / ManagedExternally or DisabledByPolicy) so apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/shell.rs:167 and the manual menu item can say why; add a settings.rs test that load honours the env var.

top.title: Backup Pass 3 (managed identities) and the enterprise-app assignee reads degrade to empty with no skipped record and no session latch
top.why: A refresh-token death or exhausted retry budget once Pass 3 begins yields an Ok manifest whose managed identities all carry held_app_roles: [] and whose enterprise apps under-report assignees, with nothing in skipped. Restore then re-binds nothing and reports success. Passes 1 and 2 were hardened for exactly this and the helper already exists.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/backup.rs:675 thread session: &SessionDead into backup_managed_identities, keep the per-item Result from batch_or_serial, call note_graph_failures on it, push SkippedObject::new("managedIdentity", ..) per Err, and mirror the post-pass `if session.is_dead() { return Err(..) }` from backup.rs:211; do the same for the assignee reads at backup.rs:555.

top.title: A >5000-site tenant's Sites.Selected sweep is truncated silently, cached for 60 minutes and reported as complete
top.why: list_all_sites drops its truncation signal, so total_sites == 5000, is_complete() is true, the per-app panel affirmatively says 'This app reaches no site through Sites.Selected' for grants on site 5001+, and the CSV coverage line claims full coverage. Every other capped scan in the crate returns (rows, truncated); this one is the exception and directly violates the 'coverage is never overstated' invariant.
top.where_to_start: crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/sharepoint.rs:105 return (Vec<Site>, truncated) mirroring collect_all_pages_capped; apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sharepoint.rs:843 bind the flag, add truncated to SiteSweepResult/AppSiteAccessDto (dto sharepoint.rs:130) and fold it into is_complete(); cache WITH the flag (do not re-sweep 5000 sites per visit) and render IndexCapNotice in views/resource_access/sites.rs and app_site_access_panel.rs.

top.title: Claims codec emits TransformationID instead of ID for transformation claims and conflates both on read
top.why: Every transformation claim the editor writes has no schema ID for its output claim to join to, so the claim is never emitted; an existing correct Microsoft-shaped policy is parsed with the transformation reference lost and re-saved pointing at a transformation that does not exist. The round-trip test masks it by using one string for all three ids. Silent breakage of federated sign-in claims, discovered only by the relying party.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sso/claims.rs:48 add transformation_id to ClaimSchemaEntryDto, always emit ID from id and TransformationID from transformation_id, read ID and TransformationID/TransformationId separately at claims.rs:204, round-trip DataType on TransformParamDto; replace the masking test (claims.rs:411) with Microsoft's documented fixture and expose the field in web-rs components/claims_editor.rs.

top.title: resolve_mail_scopes hardcodes Microsoft Graph, so EWS full_access_as_app never gets a verdict
top.why: The broadest mailbox grant that exists shows Mailbox: Unknown forever in the Permissions tab, an EWS-only app pays the Exchange consent prompt and caches an empty result, and after a successful Application EWS.AccessAsApp scoping the audit still scores the app at org-wide weight so the RBAC-scoping workflow never visibly converges. The audit direction is conservative, but the operator cannot see their work land.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/exchange/mail_scopes.rs:108 accept (value, role) pairs or ExchangeTarget (the shape get_mail_scopes_for_principal already builds at :377) instead of re-deriving the role with MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID; fix the entries filter at :341 and the audit variant at :242; correct the false rationale at mod.rs:32-35 and add a resolver test whose input is EWS-only.

top.title: Transient lookup failures are swallowed and the degraded result is cached as authoritative (permission detail and audit score_one)
top.why: A 429/5xx resolving one resource SP marks every permission on that resource 'Not granted' for the 60-minute TTL and offers to grant or delete it; a failed SP lookup in score_one skips the org-wide reconciliation so a Scoped verdict is awarded without proof and the run is cached as a clean complete scan. Both undo the graph layer's own Ok-only caching and contradict the 'degraded run is never cached' rule.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/applications/permissions_resolve.rs:277 keep Result<Option<SP>> per resource, return a degraded flag and skip state.cache.put at mod.rs:292 when set (plus a serde-defaulted resolution_degraded on ApplicationDetail for a Callout); apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/audit.rs:1489 return Err (classified Transient -> unscored -> PerPrincipalScoring) instead of None.

top.title: Permission tester reports a definitive no_access when the Graph reads failed, and its reverse lookup never sees EWS-only holders
top.why: Both the mailbox and site testers fold read failures into 'not held' and print positive statements ('holds no organization-wide SharePoint grant') they never established, contrary to the SharePoint helper's own contract and the arch doc; find_mailbox_reachers discovers candidates from the Graph resource only, so a principal with full_access_as_app over every mailbox is reported as no_access. An admin uses these answers to decide who can read a mailbox.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/permission_tester.rs:63 and :888 return a tri-state (Held / None / Unreadable, keeping SP-not-found as None) and score Unreadable as unknown in synthesize and in test_site_access at :1092; at :466 page appRoleAssignedTo on both mailbox resources via mailbox_resource_roles (or reuse prefetch_ews_full_access_grants) so EWS holders enter candidates.

top.title: Linux release builds on floating ubuntu-latest, so the AppImage/.deb need glibc 2.38+ and cannot start on Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 or RHEL 9
top.why: The .deb installs cleanly and then fails at exec on every current LTS the README says it runs on, and the floor silently moves with GitHub's runner image. Blast radius is every Linux operator on a supported-until-2027 distro.
top.where_to_start: .github/workflows/release.yml:105 pin the Linux leg to ubuntu-22.04 and add an objdump -T guard step asserting the max GLIBC_ version <= 2.35 (fail, not warn); document the floor in README.md:225 and the release body Row at release.yml:301.

top.title: Cancel flags and the throttle observer are shared across run kinds, so one Cancel stops another run's tenant write and reports it as never attempted
top.why: audit_cancel is claimed by the read-only audit, every bulk write and the AAP migration, and the keep-alive UI lets them overlap; CancelFlag::cancel stamps every older generation, so cancelling a scan halts a bulk delete or scope-and-strip mid-selection (and vice versa turns a full scan into an uncached 'cancelled early' result). The single throttle observer slot means a surviving fan-out loses adaptive back-off when the other run's guard drops.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/state.rs add bulk_cancel and migration_cancel CancelFlags and point apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/bulk.rs:127 (cancel_bulk) and the 11 bulk claim sites plus aap_migration.rs:52 at them; split sweep_cancel at permission_tester.rs:443 into site/keyvault/mailbox flags; pin command->flag in repo_invariants/cancel.rs; make the observer slot at throttle.rs:141 compare-and-clear or multi-observer.

top.title: Exchange transport and consolidation misreport writes: replayed New-/Remove- cmdlets read as failures, case-different DNs refuse a landed repoint, and a 400 can read as 'no references' before an irreversible group delete
top.why: A New-ManagementRoleAssignment that committed before a 502 is replayed, fails as a duplicate and grants.rs then keeps the org-wide grant with 'scoping is NOT effective'; a Remove-ApplicationAccessPolicy replay reports partial while the policy is gone; raw DN compares can flag a correct migration as scope_filter_mismatch; identity-less list-alls through invoke_optional can turn a misclassified 400 into an empty reference set that unlocks Remove-DistributionGroup. Each makes the reported outcome differ from the tenant.
top.where_to_start: crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/client/transport.rs:265 port send_core onto with_retries with a retry_class_for(cmdlet) helper (Get-/Test-/Search- Idempotent, New-/Remove-/Set- NonIdempotent) and extend repo_invariants/trust.rs:163 to flag raw MAX_RETRIES users; crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/targets.rs:716 and scope_group.rs:540/:744 compare folded DNs; crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/client/rbac.rs:220 and :270 switch list_management_scopes/get_application_access_policies to invoke_command.

top.title: Audit-surface fixes report success while doing nothing or dropping warnings, and the Fix button disappears
top.why: Redundant-permissions Fix returns removed: [], skipped: [] when every covering permission is vetoed (any non-Exchange-admin), the UI toasts 'Removed 0' and retains the button away while the finding and grant remain; the SP path of ScopeMailboxButton hard-codes 0 warnings so 'groups were NOT applied' reads as a clean scope; consent failures set a Callout that unmounts before it is seen. Operators trust these one-click fixes precisely because they promise to report.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/remediation.rs:257 push the value into skipped (or a vetoed list with reason) when the pre-veto set was non-empty, and in web-rs views/audit_view/row.rs:377 fire on_done only when removed is non-empty; views/dialogs/scope_remediation.rs:111 use res.warnings.len() and keep the modal open when non-empty; views/tabs/permissions_tab.rs:116 toast failures before on_changed.

themes.name: Audit blind spots and false all-clear
themes.summary: The scorer and the workbench under-report in several directions: a whole family of RBAC-scopable mailbox permissions is invisible, EWS scoping never converges, swallowed lookups are cached as clean, Exchange unavailability and unconfinable org-wide reach are scored but have no finding group or coverage caveat, and Microsoft's own disabled-app flag and federated trusts are never read. Fixes are mostly table entries plus a serde-defaulted flag per DTO.

themes.name: Coverage and truncation reported as complete
themes.summary: Several capped or partially failed scans lack a truncation/degraded dimension and are cached or rendered as authoritative: the 5000-site sweep, the permission detail resolution, Log Analytics PartialError results, inner $batch 5xx, the search corpus. The repo's own invariant ('never shown as all-clear') is the standard; the pattern is to carry (rows, truncated) and fold it into is_complete().

themes.name: Mutation outcome fidelity: what the UI reports versus what landed
themes.summary: Partial or warned writes are toasted as success, one-click destructive actions run unconfirmed, Err-after-write paths skip cache invalidation so lists go stale and retries duplicate, identifier URIs replay a stale snapshot, and the Exchange transport turns committed writes into reported failures. The established shape (outcome, Option<UiError>) and a shared is_clean predicate close most of these.

themes.name: DR backup and restore integrity
themes.summary: The DR path has the highest per-incident blast radius: non-idempotent restore with a re-run instruction, silently thin manifests, failed reads reported as runbook facts, a dry run that does not look at the destination, flexible FICs skipping the whole app, identifier URIs dropped together with scopes and pre-authorized clients, and {} written on serialization failure.

themes.name: Permission tester and reverse lookups
themes.summary: The 'who can reach this mailbox/site/vault' answers fold read failures into 'not held', miss EWS-only holders, label inherited Azure RBAC as direct vault grants and duplicate management-group assignments per subscription. Sub-site Selected grants made in the app cannot be listed or revoked in the app.

themes.name: Session, auth and secret handling
themes.summary: A domain-form tenant id is accepted but can never sign in; interaction_required purges the whole session instead of a per-resource step-up; sign_out clears memory before the fallible keyring delete; settings.json corruption is overwritten with defaults (losing vault bindings); Key Vault secret metadata survives a tenant switch; cache-only search answers without proving the session; TokenResponse has a plaintext Debug; two scoped tokens are minted with a scope set Learn says is insufficient.

themes.name: Updater, packaging and inert documented controls
themes.summary: The opt-out documented for MDM and MSI deployers is dead code, the install format is never checked, Linux artifacts cannot start on current LTS distros, macOS auto-update triggers keychain prompts the README does not mention, and a failed update check is not logged despite the README saying it is. Webview grants and CSP allowlists are wider than used.

themes.name: Concurrency, cancellation and launch cost
themes.summary: Three cancel flags are shared across run kinds that the keep-alive UI lets overlap, the throttle observer is a single overwritable slot, the halving window re-anchors, and cold launch pays several tenant-wide paginations plus every parked pane's detail fetch. Scoped writes bypass the retry loop entirely and non-Graph clients have no connect_timeout.

themes.name: Error UX, dead-session recovery and IPC robustness
themes.summary: Only a handful of UiError codes get any treatment: 24 inline-error call sites never offer Re-authenticate, unauthorized renders as bare text while three hints say 'sign out', throttled leaks Option Debug formatting, toast messages collapse the appended hint, network errors hide the cause, and a non-UiError IPC rejection panics the whole WASM app.

themes.name: Sovereign cloud and capability catalog drift
themes.summary: The SSO wizard hardcodes the commercial template id and login host although the product advertises US Gov/China; the readiness catalog lacks entries for claims mapping and provisioning scopes and cannot recognise the custom Entra role the repo itself recommends; the operator RBAC docs omit permissions behind shipped features.

quick_wins.why: One shared is_clean predicate stops a partial AAP migration reading as success on the Permissions tab.
Four prefixes plus risk-table entries make tenant-wide mailbox write score as the critical finding it is.
Two settings reads in updater.rs (with F139/F487's bundle_type gate) make the documented opt-out and the MSI/.deb policy real.
Threading SessionDead and note_graph_failures into Pass 3 reuses existing helpers and stops thin DR manifests reading as complete.
Skip cache.put when a resource SP resolution failed; stops 60 minutes of 'Not granted' for granted permissions.
Return Err instead of None on a failed SP lookup; the existing Transient classification does the rest.
One skipped.push plus gating on_done on removed.is_empty() stops the Fix button vanishing while the grant remains.
Replace the hard-coded 0 with res.warnings.len(); a copy-paste asymmetry that hides 'groups were NOT applied'.
Distinguish NotFound from parse/IO failure in mutate so a hand-edit typo cannot wipe vault bindings and tenant defaults.
One Effect on tenant.get() clearing five signals closes the only tenant-scoped surface that ignores the #1 footgun rule.
Pin ubuntu-22.04 and add an objdump guard; restores Linux operators on every current LTS.
Make is_valid_tenant GUID-only and align the config screen copy; removes a deterministic first-run dead end (or resolve the domain lazily in sign_in).
Format Retry-After properly and say to wait; the throttled message currently leaks 'retry after Some(30)s'.
Add white-space: pre-wrap to .toast__message so the Exchange/KV/ARM remediation hints actually render.
Two call sites to invoke_command so a misclassified 400 cannot unlock an irreversible group delete.
Fold DN case in three comparisons so a landed repoint is not refused as scope_filter_mismatch.
Count in the label and a ConfirmDialog before deleting every client secret of an app.
Dedupe ARM assignments by id so a management-group role is not shown N times and inflating high-privilege counts.
A wrapper that maps non-UiError rejections to a synthetic UiError turns a whole-app WASM panic into a toast.
Judge confirmed in lib.rs:340-354: the appender .expect() runs before any subscriber or panic hook, so an unwritable log dir means the app silently does not open; fall back to stderr-only logging.

strategic.title: Posture snapshot and drift report (#109)
strategic.why: Turns the audit from a point-in-time screen into 'N new high-risk grants since the last snapshot', the question a security admin actually asks; every seam is verified present and the owner's design is written, including the fail-closed rules for uncovered resources.

strategic.title: Audit signal expansion: federated trusts, Microsoft-disabled apps, risky workload identities, workload-identity CA, credential last-used
strategic.why: The workbench is blind to the credential class its own docs call the worst case (FICs), to Microsoft's own 'this app is abusive' flag, to Identity Protection risk and to CA policies that target service principals. Each is one $select field or one v1.0 read plus a table-tested rule; together they change what the audit can claim.

strategic.title: DR hardening: adoption-aware restore and destination-aware dry run
strategic.why: Make Pass 1 resolve existing apps by marker/display name so re-runs are safe, have plan_restore look at the destination and the schema, record MI Azure roles the manifest already promises, and rewrite every api:// form. This is the project that makes the DR feature trustworthy rather than a one-shot.

strategic.title: Run-identity model for cancellation, progress and throttling
strategic.why: Replace the three shared flags with claim()-returned run ids carried on progress events and a cancel_run(run_id) command, a multi-observer throttle slot and single-flight on the site sweep; fixes collateral cancellation, interleaved progress and lost back-off in one design.

strategic.title: Detail pane reactivity: stop remounting every tab on each mutation
strategic.why: The whole-pane rebuild is the root cause of unmounted outcome notes, torn-down certificate reveals, lost scroll and stale-snapshot replays; fixing it once retires several workarounds and the launch-time fetch storm from restored panes.

strategic.title: GUI coverage of mutation-heavy surfaces and degraded audit states
strategic.why: SSO wizard, federated credentials, Expose-an-API, Owners, Permissions actions and every cancelled/truncated/degraded audit rendering have zero browser tests, and the demo fixtures are unregistered or stale for 13 read commands; the frontend's only behavioural gate does not cover the paths where this review found its bugs.

strategic.title: Capability catalog completion and readiness against the recommended custom role
strategic.why: Readiness cannot recognise the custom Entra role the repo ships, claims mapping and provisioning have no catalog entry so their 403s carry no remediation and their tabs offer no consent button, and the operator RBAC docs omit permissions behind shipped features.

strategic.title: Observability and support bundle (pending verification)
strategic.why: No client-request-id is sent, request-id is not captured outside Exchange, write commands log no failures, webview panics are not persisted and there is no 'copy diagnostics' affordance; a support engineer cannot correlate a failed tenant mutation with Microsoft. Most items are still pending the second verification pass.

result.overall: The codebase is unusually explicit about its own safety invariants (never under-report, never cache a degraded run, coverage is never overstated, a partial success is a real write), and most of the serious findings are places where one path escaped the rule its neighbours obey: the mailbox advisory prefix list, the 5000-site cap, Pass 3 of the backup, the AAP migration toast, the Exchange transport that never adopted with_retries, the swallowed SP lookup. That is good news for remediation, because the fix shape already exists in the same file in almost every case, and roughly half of the top fifteen are small changes. The highest operator harm concentrates in three places: the audit scoring a tenant-wide mailbox write as healthy, the DR restore that duplicates the estate when the operator follows the on-screen remedy, and the SSO claims path that can detach a working policy from an empty editor. A fourth cluster, mutation outcome fidelity, is broader but shallower: many surfaces toast success on partial, warned or vetoed results, and the repo's own (outcome, Option<UiError>) pattern and a shared is_clean predicate would close most of them. Documented controls that do nothing (the update opt-out, the MSI policy) and a Linux artifact that cannot start on supported distros are deployment-level trust problems that a fleet admin discovers only in production. Session handling is mostly sound but has two sharp edges worth fixing early: interaction_required purging the whole session, and settings.json corruption being overwritten with defaults. Concurrency across run kinds was a genuine review blind spot and the shared cancel flags mean a read-only Cancel can halt a tenant write; the fix is small but the design (run ids) deserves a project. On the value side, the posture snapshot/drift report, federated-trust and disabled-by-Microsoft signals, and an adoption-aware restore are the enhancements that most change what an admin can rely on this tool to say. Verification quality was high: verifiers downgraded several headline claims (F140's duplicate assignment, F164, F393, F266, F001) and those corrections are reflected in the ranking; 26 observability and test-oracle findings remain pending and were kept out of the top list except F478, which I confirmed in lib.rs directly.

result.lens: Engineering leverage and maintainability: fixes that remove a class of bugs (missing invariant pins, bypassed primitives, shared helpers, seams), large-tenant performance, dependency and toolchain hygiene, documentation drift that misleads contributors, CI gaps.

top.title: Give the orchestration layer a test seam: lift ProgressSink, add commands/test_support.rs, write the partial-write tests the &GraphClient cores already allow
top.why: Roughly twenty confirmed bugs (F001, F004, F023, F037, F038, F039, F054, F070-F075, F460) sit in State- or AppHandle-bound bodies that no test can construct; only credentials.rs and backup.rs have wiremock handler tests, and bulk.rs proved the trait seam works then kept it private. One seam and one fixture module turn every future tiering, latch and fail-closed rule into a testable path instead of a review-only one.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/progress.rs:21 - move the private `trait ProgressSink` from bulk.rs:46 here as pub(crate) with `impl<R: tauri::Runtime> ProgressSink for AppHandle<R>` and a `#[cfg(test)] Recorder`; delete backup.rs:364's `&(dyn Fn(usize) + Sync)` closure in favour of it. Then add commands/test_support.rs (one /v1.0 mock base-URL convention, FIXED_NOW, sp()/app()/manifest() builders) and write the three F455 tests against permissions.rs:618, permissions.rs:389 and applications/mod.rs:329, which already take &GraphClient.

top.title: Bring the Exchange transport under the shared retry class and error taxonomy, and make the trust.rs rule flag hand-rolled loops instead of skipping them
top.why: AGENTS.md says one definition per HTTP retry and error policy, but crates/azapptoolkit-exchange open-codes both: every New-/Remove- cmdlet is replayed on 5xx or connection reset (false failures that leave org-wide grants in place per grants.rs:118), the ExchangeError ui_code table is unpinned, and repo_invariants/trust.rs:163 skips any file without `with_retries(`, so the invariant passes vacuously. Fixing the rule prevents the next client from escaping the same way.
top.where_to_start: crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/client/transport.rs:265 - replace the attempt/delay_ms loop with `with_retries(label, retry_class_for(cmdlet), |_| ...)` where Get-/Test-/Search- are Idempotent and New-/Remove-/Set- are NonIdempotent; then change apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/repo_invariants/trust.rs:163 to fail any crate source outside http_retry.rs that references MAX_RETRIES, next_backoff_ms or sleep_before_retry directly; add crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/tests/error_conformance.rs mirroring arm's (retryable set, REAUTH_FATAL_CODES survive Token, Forbidden hint from capability); fix http_retry.rs:1-3 and http_error.rs:1-2 wording.

top.title: Stop heterogeneous long runs from sharing one CancelFlag and one throttle observer slot
top.why: Three AppState flags are each shared by runs that the keep-alive UI can start concurrently (audit + bulk write + AAP migration; site sweep + KV sweep + mailbox probe; backup + restore), and CancelFlag::cancel deliberately stops every older generation, so any Cancel button halts tenant writes it never targeted. GraphClient's single throttle_observer slot is overwritten and then cleared by whichever run drops first. Pinning command-to-flag in the invariants suite makes the fix stick.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/state.rs (CancelFlag fields) and commands/bulk.rs:127 - add `bulk_cancel` and `migration_cancel`, point the 11 bulk claim sites and aap_migration.rs:52 at them, split sweep_cancel into site/keyvault/mailbox flags with their own cancel commands, and add a rule in repo_invariants/cancel.rs that a `bulk_*` body claims `bulk_cancel` and `run_audit` claims `audit_cancel`. In crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client.rs:262 make `clear_throttle_observer` compare-and-clear (`Arc::ptr_eq` against the guard's tracker, throttle.rs:140) and warn on displacement.

top.title: Capped and degraded reads must carry their signal: truncation on the site sweep, SP-lookup failure in score_one, per-MI failures in backup Pass 3
top.why: The same shape recurs: a reader hits a cap or swallows an Err, returns a clean Vec, and the caller caches or reports the result as complete (a >5000-site tenant's Sites.Selected sweep is cached as complete; an audit with a failed SP lookup caches as clean; a DR backup silently thins). collect_all_pages_capped already returns (Vec, bool) and the audit DTO already has a truncated dimension, so this is applying an existing pattern and pinning it with table tests.
top.where_to_start: crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/sharepoint.rs:74 - add `collect_pages_from_capped(first, max, fetch) -> Result<(Vec<T>, bool)>` next to transport.rs:269 (this also deletes the hand-rolled loop F186) and make list_all_sites return the flag; add `#[serde(default)] truncated: bool` to SiteSweepResult and AppSiteAccessDto (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sharepoint.rs:130) and fold it into is_complete; extract `sweep_is_cacheable` beside sharepoint.rs:988 and table-test all combinations like audit.rs:1664. Then audit.rs:1489 pushes a coverage gap on the Err arm, and backup.rs:675 takes `&SessionDead` and records `SkippedObject::new("managedIdentity", ..)`.

top.title: Pin the IPC contract mechanically and stop a non-UiError rejection from aborting the WASM app
top.why: The command name, arg-struct field and return-type parity between generate_handler![], #[tauri::command] and bindings/ is checked only by an advisory hook that always exits 0 and needs jq; the one wire type outside the DTO crate is hand-mirrored, APPS_MAX is hand-mirrored, and `invoke_result` unwraps error deserialization so any string rejection (invalid args, ACL) panics the whole frontend. A source-scan test in the existing repo_invariants idiom closes the class.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/repo_invariants/ipc.rs (new) reusing `sources::commands()` at sources.rs:133 - assert every command is registered once, every command has a `"name"` literal in web-rs/src/bindings, arg-struct fields equal the command's params, with a vacuity floor. In apps/desktop/web-rs/src/bindings/mod.rs:17 wrap `tauri_sys::core::invoke_result` to deserialize both sides through serde_json::Value and map a non-UiError rejection to `UiError::new("ipc", ..)`, then forbid direct tauri_sys imports in bindings via the same scan. Move DirectoryIndexStatus (commands/applications/mod.rs:86) into azapptoolkit-dto and add `app_index_cap`.

top.title: The updater ignores the documented opt-out and the install format
top.why: README promises `auto_update=false` / AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE means no updater traffic, yet UserSettings::load has zero production callers and check_for_update runs unconditionally; MSI and .deb installs are offered NSIS/AppImage bytes because latest.json publishes only bare platform keys and nothing reads bundle_type(). One pure `update_policy(settings, bundle_type)` function with a unit test fixes both and gives the UI an honest tri-state.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/updater.rs:26 - add `fn update_policy(auto_update: bool, bundle: Option<BundleType>) -> UpdatePolicy { Disabled | ManagedExternally(format) | Enabled }`, read `UserSettings::load(&crate::config_directory()).auto_update` and `tauri::utils::platform::bundle_type()` in both commands, short-circuit before `updater.check()`, make the DTO tri-state so shell.rs:186 can hide or relabel the manual item; unit-test the pure function and mock the new shape in the GUI shell test.

top.title: Pin the Linux release runner and add a glibc-floor guard so the artifact's minimum distro cannot drift with GitHub's image
top.why: release.yml builds the AppImage and .deb on floating ubuntu-latest (24.04, glibc 2.39); aws-lc-sys pulls strong GLIBC_2.38 imports, so Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 and RHEL 9 fail at exec while README says 'runs on most distributions'. A one-line pin plus an objdump assertion turns a silent drift into a red release job.
top.where_to_start: .github/workflows/release.yml:105 - change the Linux leg to `ubuntu-22.04` and add a post-build step `objdump -T target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/azapptoolkit | grep -oE 'GLIBC_[0-9.]+' | sort -Vu | tail -1` asserted <= 2.35; document the floor in README.md:225 and the release-body Row text, and note the pin is load-bearing in docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md:13.

top.title: Contributor gates that lie: `just setup` panics on a fresh clone, docs-only CI skips the tests that pin AGENTS.md and CHANGELOG, `just check` skips the GUI harness
top.why: The first command every doc tells a newcomer to run fails (cargo check before trunk build, with `custom-protocol` making generate_context! panic); a CHANGELOG-only or AGENTS.md-only PR merges green because release.rs's five pinning tests are skipped by the changes detector; the inner loop type-checks the frontend without --all-targets --features test-support. All three are one-line fixes with outsized trust payoff.
top.where_to_start: scripts/setup.sh:132 and scripts/setup.ps1:73 - replace the hand-typed `cargo check --workspace` with `just check` and run it after `trunk build --locked`; .github/workflows/ci.yml:75 - add `AGENTS.md|CHANGELOG.md|.claude/hooks/*) code=true ;;` ahead of the docs arm and update .claude/rules/release-and-dependencies.md:23; justfile:251 - add `--all-targets --features test-support` to the web-rs check.

top.title: Mailbox-scoping knowledge lives in two tables that disagree: resolve_mail_scopes hardcodes the Graph resource and mailbox_named misses the RBAC-era permission families
top.why: AGENTS.md's rule is 'carry the resource, never the bare value', yet mail_scopes.rs re-derives the Exchange role from MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID at three sites, so EWS full_access_as_app never gets a verdict and a correctly scoped app scores org-wide; scoping.rs's name-shaped fallback lacks MailboxItem./MailboxFolder./Mail-Advanced., so org-wide read/write of every mailbox item is all-clear. The two halves are each tested but never joined; one table test over Microsoft's RBAC roles page pins both.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/exchange/mail_scopes.rs:108 (and :242, :341) - accept `&[(resource_app_id, value)]` or `&[ExchangeTarget]` and read the role from the target instead of `exchange_role_for_resource_permission(MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID, ..)`; crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/scoping.rs:195 - extend `mailbox_named` with MailboxFolder., MailboxItem., MailboxConfigItem., Mail-Advanced. and add a table test citing the Learn application-rbac table; add the joined resolver test in commands/exchange/tests.rs:200 feeding full_access_as_app end to end.

top.title: Cache-invalidation tiering and cache-guard rules exist but are not pinned, so mis-tiers keep landing
top.why: repo_invariants/cache.rs pins that a cache-only read proves the session, but accepts `graph_for(` as proof and cannot see reads inside helpers; nothing pins which invalidator a command may call (bulk.rs:283 and four SSO detail writes bust both tenant-wide indexes, costing a full app + SP re-enumeration on large tenants), nor that the CacheKind::Audit put sits behind run_is_cacheable. Two more source-scan rules make the documented tiers self-enforcing.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/bulk.rs:283 - replace `invalidate_app_lists` with a loop over `invalidate_app_credentials` (or an `_many` variant); commands/sso/mod.rs:707, :746, :1662, :1728 - use `invalidate_app_details`; then in tests/repo_invariants/cache.rs add (a) `invalidate_app_lists(` allowed only in bodies that also call create_/delete_/ensure_service_principal/rename, (b) every `.put(CacheKind::Audit` must be inside an `if run_is_cacheable(` block, and (c) drop `graph_for(` from SESSION_PROOFS at cache.rs:564 and match the cached-accessor helper names, adding `prove_tenant_session` to search.rs:302, :235 and applications/mod.rs:108.

top.title: Frontend primitives are bypassed at scale (Badge 45 sites, DataTable 15 raw tables, DetailLoadError ~10 tabs, DirectorySearch 2 owners tabs) with no pin, so the a11y and 'No matches' bugs they were built to end have come back
top.why: AGENTS.md says one primitive per UI pattern, reuse never re-implement; the code has the primitives and also the copies, including a `badge--info` tone that does not exist in CSS and an owners search that reintroduces the documented untouched-box bug. Making Badge.tone an enum and adding three source-scan rules (precedent: repo_invariants/commands.rs scans frontend sources) prevents recurrence while the migrations are mechanical.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/web-rs/src/components/badge.rs - make `tone` an enum (Neutral|Ok|Warning|Danger|Critical|Info|Unknown) and add `.badge--info` to styles.css; then add a frontend source scan (in src-tauri/tests/repo_invariants or a web-rs host test) rejecting `"badge badge--` outside badge.rs, `<table class="data-table">` in a file without `use_grid_keynav`, and `Err(e) =>` rendering `form-error` inside a Suspend; migrate owners_tab.rs:457 and enterprise .../owners.rs:32 to DirectorySearch and access.rs:190 to DetailLoadError as the first batch.

top.title: The GUI and demo test infrastructure has structural blind spots: no ARIA-state assertion, no degraded-run fixture, no scan of fallible demo reads, 11 copies of click_button
top.why: The browser GUI tests are the frontend's only behavioural gate, yet no test asserts an aria-* value or live role (the boolean-attribute bug recurred twice), every Security fixture is a complete run so the 'never shown as all-clear' invariant is unpinned, demo_fixture_coverage scans only infallible invokes non-recursively and counts comment mentions as registrations, and helper drift makes tests inconsistent. Each fix is small and each prevents a class.
top.where_to_start: apps/desktop/web-rs/tests/gui/security_findings.rs:109 - add cancelled/truncated/degraded fixtures asserting the caveat strings; tests/gui/shell.rs - assert `aria-expanded="true"`/`aria-pressed` literals after toggling; tests/demo_fixture_coverage.rs:93 - add a second test over `invoke_result` literals, walk src/ recursively and strip `//` comments before the contains check; move click_button_labelled/has_button_labelled/focused_matches into src/test_support.

top.title: Inject the browser opener so sign_in, reauthenticate and the tid/nonce checks are testable, then settle the domain-form tenant id
top.why: run_auth_code_flow hard-wires open_system_browser and a private listener, so the security-relevant branches (tid mismatch, nonce mismatch, consent identity) have no end-to-end test and the domain-configured tenant that the config screen advertises has failed every sign-in since it shipped without anyone noticing. The seam is also the prerequisite for testing the CAE cache-key and interaction_required fixes.
top.where_to_start: crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:263 - add `browser: Box<dyn Fn(&str) -> Result<()> + Send + Sync>` with a `with_browser_opener` constructor; a test opener parses redirect_uri/state/nonce and hits the loopback with `GET /?code=..&state=..`, wiremock /token returns an id_token with chosen tid/oid/nonce. Then either make `is_valid_tenant` GUID-only (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/config.rs:44, web-rs config_screen.rs:125) or resolve the domain via openid-configuration at sign_in and persist the GUID so remembered_account_for matches.

top.title: Error codes are produced consistently but consumed inconsistently: consent_required flattened inside clients, a duplicated code table, Option Debug in the throttled message, toasts collapsing hints, no connect_timeout outside Graph
top.why: Each is a one-file change on a shared path (core::reauth, http_error_enum!, token_adapter, .toast__message, the four reqwest builders, CommandState::run) and each currently produces an operator-visible defect on every surface at once: scoped calls never trigger the consent fallback, 429s read 'retry after Some(30)s', Exchange/KV/ARM hints render as one line, a firewalled host spins four minutes uncancellable, 24 inline-error call sites never offer Re-authenticate.
top.where_to_start: crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/reauth.rs - add PASSTHROUGH_CODES = REAUTH_FATAL_CODES + consent_required and use it in http_error.rs:129; http_error.rs:76 - manual Display for Throttled ('Wait {n} s, then retry'); apps/desktop/web-rs/styles.css:3513 - `white-space: pre-wrap` on .toast__message; add `core::http_client::builder(total)` setting connect_timeout(10 s) and use it in arm/client.rs:38, arm/loganalytics.rs:29, exchange/client.rs:76, keyvault/client.rs:56; token_adapter.rs:19 - derive the code from `UiError::from(err).code` or pin agreement with a test; use_command.rs:85 - call `report_if_session_dead` first.

top.title: The architecture docs are the contract every agent reads, and several load-bearing sentences are wrong
top.why: AGENTS.md routes every contributor to docs/architecture before editing a subsystem, so a stale rationale is an instruction to reintroduce a bug: auth-and-consent.md says the BearerProvider boundary flattens to String and to extend two matches! sets that no longer exist; AGENTS.md claims trust.rs pins SAML cert lifetimes and that a bundled permissions catalog with Graph fallback exists (the crate holds six resource names); exchange-scoping.md documents deleted value-only functions; the ScopeWizard doc promises three touch points where ten branch. Fixing these is cheap and stops drift from compounding.
top.where_to_start: docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md:82 and :118 - rewrite to the true statements (TokenError with code; `core::reauth::REAUTH_FATAL_CODES` is the single set); AGENTS.md:108 qualify the macro rule or migrate Exchange, :112 and :122 correct the catalog and trust.rs claims; docs/architecture/caching-and-search.md:166 count nine drops; docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md:33 remove the deleted functions; apps/desktop/web-rs/src/components/scope_wizard.rs:83 list the real branch points; decide direction (a) for crates/azapptoolkit-permissions (rename to a resource directory and delete the dead lookup ladder rung at permissions_resolve.rs:25).

themes.name: Untestable orchestration layer
themes.summary: State- and AppHandle-bound command bodies, a hard-wired browser launcher and per-file hand-rolled fixtures mean the rules that matter (invalidate only on Ok, latch a dead session, fail closed, do not replay writes) are checked by review alone; roughly twenty confirmed bugs live exactly there. Lifting ProgressSink, adding test_support.rs, injecting the browser opener and writing the missing wiremock cases against cores that already take &GraphClient is the highest-leverage work in the report.

themes.name: Invariant suite with vacuous or module-granular rules
themes.summary: repo_invariants is the repo's best idea, but several rules pass vacuously: trust.rs checks the validator per module not per command and skips files without with_retries, cache.rs accepts graph_for( as a session proof and cannot see reads inside helpers, nothing pins IPC parity, $top, the Audit put guard, the token_error code table or the tauri-cli pin. Each fix is a small edit to an existing test file in the repo's own idiom.

themes.name: Shared policy bypassed by a second copy
themes.summary: The Exchange transport and error enum, scoped Graph writes, the AAD token call, four reqwest builders and a dozen desktop helpers re-implement policy that core or a sibling module already defines (retry class, connect timeout, 404-to-None, nextLink paging, SharePoint error mapping, strip loops). Consolidating onto the existing definition removes the drift surface and usually the bug with it.

themes.name: Coverage and degradation signals dropped
themes.summary: A reader hits a cap, swallows an Err or folds a failed read into 'not held', and the caller caches or displays the result as complete or all-clear: the site sweep, the audit SP lookup, backup Pass 3, the permission tester's EntraReach, Log Analytics PartialError, the AAP migration toast. The fix pattern is the same everywhere: carry the signal in the type, include it in is_complete or is_clean, exclude it from the cache, table-test the predicate, render the caveat.

themes.name: Concurrency across run kinds and adaptive throttle
themes.summary: The docstrings assume long runs never overlap, but keep-alive views and per-component busy flags let them; shared CancelFlags cancel each other, one throttle observer slot is overwritten, the halving window re-anchors so the cap halves once, list_applications_with_pairing bypasses the single-flight gate and the grant read-through cache is attached to the wrong read. Per-run identity plus a pinned command-to-flag mapping is the durable fix.

themes.name: Cache tiering and invalidation on partial writes
themes.summary: Credential- and detail-only writes bust both tenant-wide indexes (a full app + SP re-enumeration on large tenants), several cached lists have no mutation-driven invalidation, refresh of Managed Identities is a no-op, and cores that return Err after a landed write skip invalidation entirely. A source-scan rule on which invalidator a command may call, plus the (outcome, Option<UiError>) shape the file already uses elsewhere, closes the class.

themes.name: Frontend primitives bypassed and a11y state unpinned
themes.summary: Badge, DataTable, DetailLoadError, DirectorySearch and ModalShell exist and are documented as the single home for their pattern, yet dozens of hand-rolled copies ship without keyboard navigation, live regions or accessible names, and the documented boolean-attribute bug recurred twice. An enum tone, three source-scan rules and a handful of GUI assertions on exact ARIA strings make the primitives the path of least resistance.

themes.name: Dependency, toolchain and CI hygiene
themes.summary: Six unused dependencies, a bytes pin outside the workspace table, a broken keyring-core alias, a future-incompat hard error hiding under leptos_macro, no unused-dependency or rustdoc gate, a docs-only detector that skips the pinning tests, a setup script that panics on a fresh clone and a floating Linux runner that sets the glibc floor. Most are one-line fixes; cargo-machete and a glibc guard step prevent recurrence.

themes.name: Documentation drift in the agent-facing contract
themes.summary: AGENTS.md and docs/architecture are read by every agent before editing, so stale rationales about the BearerProvider boundary, the reauth code sets, the permissions catalog, the deleted value-only scoping functions, cache drop counts and the ScopeWizard's touch points actively mislead. Each is an S fix; batching them per deep-dive while touching the subsystem is the practical route.

themes.name: Error surface end to end
themes.summary: The backend emits a stable code set but the frontend branches on a handful, consent_required is flattened to token_error inside clients, throttled leaks Option Debug text, toasts collapse the hint newline, 401 tells operators to sign out against the in-place design, and only Graph has a connect timeout. Fixing the shared producers (reauth passthrough, macro Display, one http_client builder) and the shared sink (report_command_error_for, CommandState::run) reaches every surface at once.

themes.name: Capabilities catalog is the one definition but has holes
themes.summary: Readiness keeps a hardcoded CAE list that drifted from the catalog, claims-mapping and provisioning scopes have no entry (so 403s carry no remediation and the provisioning pane cannot offer consent), the custom Entra role the repo recommends is not recognised, and the operator-role docs omit the directory permissions behind rollover and claims. Adding the missing entries and deriving the probe list from the catalog restores the single definition.

quick_wins.why: Two-line change in scripts/setup.sh and setup.ps1 makes the first documented command succeed on a fresh clone on all three OSes.
One `case` arm in ci.yml runs the five AGENTS.md/CHANGELOG/hook pinning tests on exactly the PRs that can break them.
Pin ubuntu-22.04 plus an objdump guard step; stops shipping Linux binaries that cannot start on Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 or RHEL 9.
Gating check_for_update on UserSettings::load(..).auto_update honours a documented enterprise deploy promise with a pure function and a test (ship with F139).
Adding --all-targets --features test-support to justfile:251 makes the inner loop compile what CI compiles, catching GUI-harness breaks in seconds.
Separate last_halved from last_throttle in throttle.rs:102 so the adaptive cap actually degrades under a sustained 429 storm; paused-clock test included.
Compare-and-clear on clear_throttle_observer (Arc::ptr_eq) stops one fan-out from silently removing another's back-off.
Loop invalidate_app_credentials instead of invalidate_app_lists after the expired-credential sweep; avoids a full app + SP re-enumeration on every bulk sweep.
Three prove_tenant_session calls plus dropping graph_for( from SESSION_PROOFS make the cache-read invariant real instead of vacuous.
A source-scan pin that the CacheKind::Audit put sits behind run_is_cacheable turns an AGENTS.md sentence into a failing test.
Refusing to overwrite an unparseable settings.json (or renaming it .corrupt first) prevents permanent loss of vault bindings and tenant defaults on the next sign-in.
A shared `AapMigrationReport::is_clean()` used by both surfaces stops a partial migration from toasting Migrated and makes the two surfaces unable to disagree.
Deserializing the IPC rejection through serde_json::Value first turns a whole-app WASM panic into a normal UiError toast.
Manual Display for the Throttled arm removes 'retry after Some(30)s' from every Graph/ARM/KV/Exchange surface in one macro edit.
One CSS line (`white-space: pre-wrap` on .toast__message) makes every Exchange/KV/ARM hint readable.
connect_timeout(10 s) on the four non-Graph builders turns a four-minute uncancellable spinner into a ten-second failure.
Exhaustive match in CacheKind::idx plus a const assert makes a new cache kind a compile error instead of a runtime index panic inside a command.
Deriving token_adapter's code from UiError::from(err) collapses a hand-copied table the repo already built core::reauth to avoid.
Removing six dead dependency declarations plus a cargo-machete recipe (F213) with the thiserror ignore means the next one fails CI at the PR that adds it.
Two paragraphs in auth-and-consent.md currently instruct agents to do the wrong thing at the BearerProvider boundary and the reauth code set.

strategic.title: Detail-pane and launch-time state architecture
strategic.why: Every mutation rebuilds the whole detail pane and remounts every visited tab (the root cause behind three deferred-reload workarounds and the certificate-reveal teardown), a restored dock mounts every parked pane and fires its full Graph fetch before Home paints, and Home ships the entire cached audit run over IPC to render counts. A long-lived RwSignal<Arc<ApplicationDetail>> outside the Suspend, first-show gating of restored windows and a get_cached_audit_summary command are one coherent project with measurable large-tenant payoff.

strategic.title: Behavioural GUI coverage for the mutation-heavy surfaces
strategic.why: The browser tests are the frontend's only behavioural gate, yet Owners, Expose an API, Permissions actions, rotate/new-secret/federated flows, the SSO wizard, create app and enterprise Access have zero coverage, and no test renders a degraded run or asserts an ARIA state. A shared helper module plus one shard per surface would have caught F333, F340, F371, F372 and F394 before shipping.

strategic.title: Run identity for cancellation and progress channels
strategic.why: Beyond the minimal per-kind flags in the top list, the robust design is for claim() to return a generation that rides the first progress event as run_id, a cancel_run(run_id) command that stops exactly one run, and listeners that filter by run_id; that also fixes interleaved bulk-progress rows across multiple mounted BulkActionBars and gives the AAP migration a real Cancel.

strategic.title: One HTTP transport core for the four clients
strategic.why: ARM and Key Vault duplicate the status-to-variant closure, Exchange keeps a hand-rolled enum and loop, only Graph has a connect timeout, error bodies flow raw and uncapped, network errors drop their cause, and (pending verification) no client sends client-request-id or captures request-id. A core::http_client builder plus a shared transport generic over the macro-generated error enum removes four copies of every future policy change.

strategic.title: Idempotent, honest DR restore
strategic.why: The restore report and the DR view both tell the operator to re-run, but Pass 1 creates every app unconditionally, the dry run skips the schema check and the enterprise/MI counts, identifier-URI rewriting handles one form, and a failed Graph read is reported as a runbook fact. Resolving each manifest app in the destination before creating it and threading read failures into ManualItem reasons is a bounded project that makes the DR feature trustworthy.

strategic.title: Capabilities catalog completeness and readiness derived from it
strategic.why: Readiness cannot recognise the custom Entra role the repo itself recommends, keeps a hand-maintained CAE list that already drifted, and lacks entries for claims mapping and provisioning, so 403s on those surfaces carry no remediation and the provisioning pane cannot offer consent. Adding the entries and deriving the probe list from the catalog restores the one-definition rule across the three auth planes.

strategic.title: Observability baseline (pending verification)

result.overall: This is a well-governed codebase whose distinguishing strength, a source-scanning invariants suite plus an agent-facing contract in AGENTS.md and docs/architecture, is also where the highest-leverage gaps sit: several rules pass vacuously (trust.rs skips files without with_retries and checks validators per module, cache.rs accepts a client factory as a session proof, nothing pins IPC parity, invalidation tiering, the Audit put guard or the token code table), and a handful of load-bearing doc sentences now instruct contributors to do the wrong thing. The single biggest structural issue is testability: State- and AppHandle-bound command bodies, a hard-wired browser launcher and per-file fixtures mean roughly twenty confirmed bugs (partial writes without invalidation, swallowed SP lookups, an unlatched backup pass, the EWS resolver, the claims codec, the domain tenant id) live in code no test could construct, even though bulk.rs already proved the ProgressSink seam and three cores already take &GraphClient. The second is a recurring shape across backend and frontend: a shared definition exists (retry class, error taxonomy, Badge, DataTable, DetailLoadError, DirectorySearch, the capabilities catalog) and a second hand-rolled copy drifted, with no pin to stop the third. Concurrency assumptions written into docstrings ('the two never run at once') are false under keep-alive views, so cancel flags and the throttle observer need per-run identity. Coverage signals are dropped at caps and swallowed errors and then cached or shown as complete, which for a security tool is the most consequential class here (F178, F023, F039, F394). Toolchain and CI hygiene is mostly good but has sharp edges: setup panics on a fresh clone, docs-only PRs skip the tests that pin the docs, the Linux release floor floats with ubuntu-latest, and six dead dependencies plus a future-incompat warning sit unguarded. Large-tenant performance findings are few but real: two tenant-wide index busts on credential- and detail-only writes, an ungated pairing list, a mis-attached grant cache, eager mounting of every restored pane, and the full audit run shipped over IPC for counts. Most of the top items are S or M and each closes a class rather than a symptom; the strategic projects (pane state architecture, GUI coverage of mutation surfaces, one HTTP transport core, idempotent restore) are where the remaining L effort should go.
